name: Shop
description: A keeper with a price list: things to buy for the currency, and prices paid for things out of the bag. It owns the list: what each shop sells, for how much and how many, and what it will take off the player and for what. It owns the moment of the trade: it takes the money through economy.currency and announces the purchase, or takes the thing out of inventory.core_inventory and announces the sale. It puts nothing in the bag or the purse itself: a purchase and a sale are each announced as a `reward` carrying `grants`, and the bag and the purse take what is theirs the way they take a quest's pay. It owns no words and no place: a dialogue answer whose `act` is {shop: id} opens it, a runtime may open it directly, and who stands close enough to trade is the runtime's to say. It draws nothing; it publishes what a panel needs.

implementations.note: Implemented in the consuming application; not verifiable from this repository.

inputs.name: shops
inputs.description: Who sells here: [{id, name, says?, sells, buys}]. `sells` is [{item, price, stock?}]: `stock` is how many there are to buy, and a ware without one never runs out. `buys` is [{item, price}]: what the keeper pays for one of that kind out of the bag. `says` is a line for whatever shows the shop. A kind carried with one word in front of its name (a `magic dagger`) is bought as that kind, for more; see `rarityWorth`. The last copy of a thing the player is wearing is not for sale, asked of combat.equipment_slots where the build has one. A purchase the bag has no slot for is refused before the money is taken, asked of inventory.slotted_bag where the build has one. An answer in ui.dialogue_box whose `act` is {shop: id} opens that shop.

inputs.name: rarityWorth
inputs.description: What a kind is worth to a keeper with that word in front of its name, as a multiple of the price it buys the plain kind for, rounded. A word not named here is worth the plain price.

outputs.name: shops
outputs.description: Every shop as {id, name, says, open}.

outputs.name: open
outputs.description: The id of the shop that is open, or null. One at a time.

outputs.name: wares
outputs.description: wares(id): what that shop sells now, as [{item, price, left, affordable}]. `left` is null for a ware that never runs out.

outputs.name: offers
outputs.description: offers(id): what the player carries that the shop will buy, as [{item, count, price}], one row a carried kind. The last copy of a worn thing is left out.

outputs.name: openShop
outputs.description: openShop(id): opens that shop, announced as economy.shopOpened; false for an unknown one.

outputs.name: close
outputs.description: close(): shuts the open shop, announced as economy.shopClosed; false when none is open.

outputs.name: buy
outputs.description: buy(id, item): takes the price and announces economy.itemBought, or refuses with economy.tradeRefused; true when it went through.

outputs.name: sell
outputs.description: sell(id, item): takes one of that carried kind out of the bag and announces economy.itemSold, or refuses with economy.tradeRefused; true when it went through.

provenance: Requested from play, 2026-10-02: quests in the dungeon crawler pay gold and nothing took it. Searched first (shop, vendor, merchant, buy, sell): the catalogue trades between players (social.trade_window, social.trade_coordinator, social.home_trade_stand), sells furniture back (housing.furnish_mode) and buys producers (economy.auto_producer); nothing sells a thing for the currency or buys one out of the bag. This is NOT social.trade_window: there is no second player and no offer to agree.
